exitCode.description: Only when the runner reports one or the output says "Exit code N".

Activity.description: What a lane is doing now, literally.

oneOf.description: The command's first line, `cd x &&` stripped.
Repo-relative.
A file read, or a search when `pattern` is set.
Assistant text streamed in the last 3 s.
A run is active with nothing open and no text for 3 s: waiting on the model.

AgentLane.description: One agent of an order: a task, or the project's lead.

profile.description: What it runs on: a task's own profile; a lead is always high. Absent from older hubs.

statusReason.description: Queued, parked or failed: why, e.g. "fleet cap: 40 of 40 running", "usage limit: resumes 14:05".

AgentRow.description: One agent: a task, or a project's lead, with its project.

profile.description: What it runs on: a task's own profile; a lead is always high. Absent from older hubs.

statusReason.description: Queued, parked or failed: why, e.g. "fleet cap: 40 of 40 running", "usage limit: resumes 14:05".

workstreamId.description: The work it belongs to; `live { focus }` with it streams this agent's text too. Absent for a lead.

before.description: Pass back as `before` for the page before this one; absent when there is nothing older.

running.description: A run of it is active now.

message.description: A denial's reason, passed to the lead.

dataB64.description: Standard base64; at most 5 MiB decoded.

AttachmentRef.description: A file on a message: what the app shows without fetching it. Its bytes come from `attachment_get`.

Attention.description:
Whether an event needs the human now, set by the hub when it emits the event. "loud": notify, but hold it through
quiet hours; "urgent": notify even during quiet hours (money and irreversible). Absent: the inbox and the digest
are enough.

cap.description: The fleet cap: agents running at once across every project. Needs an admin key.

pauseExtras.description:
Lowering: tell the agents above the new max to push their work in progress and wait; they resume when a slot
frees. Without it they finish their current work.

Category.description: Which color a span gets in every view, and which breakdown row it adds to.

oneOf.description: Waiting on the machine or the provider: retries, startup, compaction, claude-local time.
Waiting on a person.
CI, review and the merge train.
A session alive with no run and nobody waiting on it. Never on a critical path.

kinds.description: The same total by kind, e.g. `change.ci`, `change.review` and `change.queue` within pipeline.

lastError.description: The refusal fix, conflicting paths, or failing check names.

mergedSha.description: The squash commit on the base; set on merge.

position.description: 0-based index into its train's queue; absent when not queued.

taskId.description: The write task that opened it; absent when the lead enqueued a PR no task wrote.

ChangeReview.description: One review verdict, valid for exactly this patch. A clean rebase that keeps the patch id keeps it valid.

oneOf.description:
An agent or integration writing with its own key (`fleetd chat` with an agent key): input for the lead, never
the human. It approves nothing, answers nothing that is the human's, and leaves needs-you as it was.
fleetd itself: one-line events (a PR merged, an agent started, a past order's state).

ChatClient.description: Where a human message was written.

oneOf.description: The desktop app.
`fleetd chat`.

ChatDelivery.description: How a human message reached the lead.

oneOf.description: The lead was idle: the message started its next turn.
The lead was mid-turn: it takes the message at its next step, as a steer.
The lead is starting, or its machine is away: the message waits and goes in as soon as it can.

moreAfter.description: More messages after the last one of this page.

moreBefore.description: More messages before the first one of this page.

ChatHistorySource.description:
Where a history message came from, for messages from before the chat existed (a read model; nothing is moved or
destroyed). Absent on messages written in the chat.

oneOf.description: An order's text as it was submitted.
A person's note on an order.
A person's steer to the lead or one of its agents.
What the lead said in its own session.
An order's outcome (done, stopped, failed) as a one-line event.
A question the lead asked with the retired questions tool, and its answer.

ChatItem.description: The two things a chat can't carry as plain text, shown inline in place of the message text.

by.description: The name of the key that wrote it: a person's device for a human message, the agent for an agent's.

client.description: A human message: where it was written.

clientRequestId.description: A human message: the `clientRequestId` its `chat_send` carried, for the app's optimistic copy.

delivery.description: A human message: how it reached the lead.

history.description: From before the chat: where this history message came from.

text.description: Markdown. Empty while a streamed message has no text yet, and for an inline `item`.

updatedAt.description: Set when the text was last appended to, or an item's state changed.

oneOf.description: The lead is still writing it: `chat_delta` frames append to its text until it is `final`.

client.description: A human key: where it is written. Absent means the app.

session.description:
Sent from inside a fleetd session: its thread id (FLEETD_THREAD_ID), as the caller reports it. The project's own
lead and tasks are refused (they use their fleetd tools), and so is a human key. It catches mistakes; the key,
not this field, carries authority.

leadWaiting.description: Why the lead doesn't have it yet, with the fix; absent when it does or is starting.

message.description: The system line it wrote into the chat.

stopped.description: Something was running and stopped: the lead's turn or an agent.

ChecksState.description: The checks on the PR's head, rolled up: any failed is `failing`, else any running is `pending`.

oneOf.description: No checks ran on it.

criticalExcessMs.description: Time this check added on critical paths past the second-latest check.

requiredChecks.description: Status checks the default branch requires, from branch protection and rulesets.

workflows.description: Active GitHub Actions workflows by name (from `.github/workflows` on a checkout without GitHub access).

CloneTarget.description: Where a clone would go on a machine, and what is there now.

projectId.description: The existing directory is already this project.

sameRemote.description: The existing directory is a checkout of the same repository: `project_add` with `useExisting` adds it.

CommandApprovalItem.description:
A risky command (prod write, spend, delete, credential use) or a session's permission prompt waits for the
human: the exact command, then Approve or Deny. Answered with `approval_answer`, naming `requestId`. Exactly one of
`gated` and `permission`.

by.description: The key name of the person who answered.

finishedAt.description: Once it ran or failed: when the result came back.

gated.description: A gated command: exactly what runs once approved.

machineId.description: Where it runs, or the machine of the session that asks.

note.description: Why it is open again ("not run: the node was offline when approved"), or why it failed without running.

outputTail.description: The end of the output, once it ran.

permission.description: A session's permission prompt: the tool and what it would do.

playbook.description: A retro playbook change (an older approval only): what changes, in plain words, and the exact diff.

oneOf.description: Approved and run: see `exitCode` and `outputTail`.
Approved, and the node could not run it.

totalMs.description: Per call: each call's own interval, which may overlap others.

CommitSha.description: Full lowercase hex commit SHA, 40 or 64 characters

capped.description: The read hit its span cap and kept the newest spans.

detailSince.description:
Spans are kept only from here (retention): span lists, commands, CI checks and insights start here, while
category totals before it come from the daily roll-ups.

nothingRunningMs.description: Time with nothing running, which points at missing data.

segments.description: Oldest first; they add up to `end_ms - start_ms`.

segmentsTruncated.description: True when the order had more segments than fit; the totals still cover them all.

oneOf.description: The node's own policy, at once.
A project tool rule on the hub.

by.description: Who recorded it: the agent key name, "lead:<machineId>/<projectId>" or "human:<device>".

supersedes.description: The earlier active decision on the same key and scope that this one replaced.

DecisionSource.description: Filled by the hub from the caller: a human device, an agent key, or a lead-side call.

decisions.description: Best match first; active decisions only.

DeliveredHow.description: How a delivered steer was taken in.

oneOf.description: It started a turn while the agent was idle.
After the running tool returned.
⌘Enter stopped the running step (`stoppedTool` names it).
An older claude merged it into the running turn; the ack rule catches a miss.

DiffLine.description: One line of a file's diff. Secrets are replaced by `[secret]`.

cut.description: The line was longer than `PR_DIFF_LINE_MAX` and is cut.

new.description: Line number in the new file (context and added lines; a hunk's start).

old.description: Line number in the old file (context and deleted lines; a hunk's start).

oneOf.description: A hunk header ("@@ -12,7 +12,9 @@ fn main"); `text` is its trailing context.

fix.description: Absent when there is nothing to do.

DoctorFix.description: `auto`: doctor_fix runs it. `manual`: a person runs `command` (where the label says).

check.description: The check, run again after the fix.

ran.description: What the fix did, in plain words.

checks.description: Hub checks first, then each machine's, in a fixed order.

DoctorStatus.description: `unknown`: the hub could not look (machine offline, nothing to read).

oneOf.description: Work was added (a scope-change marker).
A review blocked: the item fell back to "PR open".
CI failed: the item fell back a stage.
A done item reopened when a later check failed.
An agent ended with nothing else in flight for its item: the item's in-stage credit is taken back.

Effort.description: The `--effort` claude runs at. Only [`TaskProfile`] picks one; nothing takes an effort as input.

Enforcement.description: Who keeps a safety rule when the prompt no longer says it.

oneOf.description: fleetd refuses the action anyway; agents just stop being told why.
Only the prompt says it; nothing else enforces it.

cursor.description: Absent means start at the current end.

attention.description: Latest failed, waiting and usage-limited events, and PRs the merge train sent back to their authors.

chats.description: Each project's chat: whether its lead waits on you, whether it works. Absent from hubs without chat.

notify.description: When to notify the human; absent from older hubs.

slots.description: Absent until the hub runs the slot board (M5).

FoundRepo.description: A git checkout found on a machine (under ~/src, ~/code, ~/projects, ~/dev and similar, at most two levels down).

projectId.description: Set when the checkout is already a project.

repo.description: When the remote is on GitHub.

oneOf.description: The node runs a fleetd without the span outbox.
The node's outbox passed its 7-day or 500k-row bound and dropped its oldest spans.
The hub's span writer was full.
A session lane with no node spans.
The critical path found time with nothing running.

GatedRunSpec.description: Stored with the approval and never changed: the human approves exactly these bytes.

GitHubCandidate.description: A repository `gh repo list` returned, for the user or one of their orgs.

checkouts.description: Machines that already have a checkout of it.

ghOn.description: Where gh ran: "hub" (the hub machine) or a machine id. Absent when gh is logged in nowhere.

owners.description: The login and the orgs listed, in order.

HubBusyItem.description: One thing in flight on the hub.

machineId.description: Where it runs, when on one machine.

text.description: What it is, for a person: "T19 writing app-main in fleetd (12 m)".

oneOf.description: A running task.
A lead turn in progress.
A merge train step: a change at the head of its train.
An approval being answered.
A project being cloned.

HubChannel.description: The release channel a hub's build follows: nightly when its version contains "-nightly.", stable otherwise.

data.description: At most 2 KB of JSON; the hub trims before emitting.

oneOf.description: The machine's node woke from sleep; `data.fromMs`, `data.toMs` (epoch milliseconds).

The machine's disk or load stopped new agents there, or no longer does; `data.paused`, and the summary says
why. Agents already running keep going.
The node no longer has the project: the hub dropped it from its cache, and its open workstreams stop. `data.title`.
A project was added from a path or a finished clone: `data` is `ProjectAddedData` (the inspect line included).

A clone `project_add` accepted is running: `data` is `CloneProgressData`. Throttled; never stored past the
event log's own retention.
A clone `project_add` accepted failed: `data` is `ProjectAddFailedData`, with the fix.
A project's settings changed (`project_set`): `data.mediumAllowed`.
Needs approval or user input.
A wake missed while the hub was down, with catchUp "skip".
A queued write to an offline machine was delivered when it came back.
A queued write outlived its TTL and was dropped.
The brief was set and the work started.
A lead needs a person for a secret or an approval; `data` is the request (RequestEventData).

A request changed state (stored, declined, approved, running, done, failed, denied, or open again when it could
not run); `data` as request.opened.
`data.queuedReason`.
A project's max agents or the fleet cap changed; `data` is `tasks::AgentsCapData`, `summary` the chat's line.
The lead closed it. `data.workstreamId`, `data.reason` (why) and `data.by`.
`data.taskId`, `data.prHeadSha`, `data.blocking`.
`data.changeId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`.
A clean review is bound to its current patch id. `data.changeId`.
The rebase conflicted; `data.changeId`, `data.paths`.
`data.changeId`, `data.checks` (failing check names), `data.logUrl`.

`data.changeId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`, `data.mergedSha`; `data.ci` when the repo had no CI and the
train merged on fleetd's own checks.

A PR was merged into a base the train guards without the train; `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`,
`data.mergedSha`, and `data.changeId` when it had been enqueued.

Something that is not the train's sits where its worktree goes, and a person has to move it; `data.changeId`,
`data.repo`, `data.error` (what to move).
Refused at enqueue; `data.prUrl`, `data.fix`.
M4: a machine's login hit the same limit on several threads, or its proxy has no account; dispatch there pauses.
M4: parked threads were sent "continue" at their reset or on usage_resume; `data.breakerCleared`.
M11: doctor checks changed status; `data.changes` lists `{ id, from, to }` (from absent on the first run).
A device redeemed a pairing code from `fleetd pair` and got a human key; `data.keyId`, `data.deviceName`.

A prompt override was saved or reset: `data.id`, `data.scope`, `data.projectRef`, `data.ref` (absent on reset),
`data.warnings` (their codes). The text is not in the event; prompt_get reads it.

This release changed the default of a prompt you overrode; yours stays in effect until you save it again or
reset it: `data.id`, `data.scope`, `data.projectRef`, `data.base`, `data.current`.

A steer was stored (or put in the offline queue). `data` is a `SteerEventData`, plus `data.text` (first 120
characters), `data.mode` and `data.by`.
claude took the steer in; `data.how`.
The agent replied after taking it in (`data.excerpt`), or a lead call named it.
The steer's run ended with no reply after it was delivered.

Refused by the node, the process exited before taking it in, or it expired in the offline queue;
`data.reason`.
A plan's scope changed and a marker was written; `data` is the `PlanChange` (`status::PlanChangedData`).
The hub verified a plan item done; `data.itemId`, `data.milestoneId`, `data.workstreamId`, `data.evidence`.

A merge-train Change moved between states; `data.changeId`, `data.workstreamId`, `data.repo`, `data.prNumber`,
`data.from`, `data.to`.
Main-branch CI of a train repo changed state; `data.repo`, `data.sha`, `data.state`, `data.failing`.
A status source went quiet past its cadence; `data.source`, `data.sinceMs`, `data.reason`.
A stale source answered again; `data.source`, `data.staleMs`.

A project's chat got a message, or one of its messages finished streaming or had an inline item change state;
`data` is `chat::ChatMessageEventData`.

A project's chat started or stopped waiting on you, or its lead started or ended a turn; `data` is the
`chat::ProjectChatState`.

machineId.description: Only what runs on this machine (before restarting its node); absent: everything.

busy.description: Empty when nothing is in flight. A restart interrupts each item.

version.description: The hub's fleetd version, as `fleetd --version` prints it. "0.0.0" for a local build.

HumanRequest.description: One human request, as stored and as every client shows it.

evidence.description:
What happened, in one line: "fingerprint ab12cd34", "exit 0 on devbox, approved by human:desk", or why it did
not run (and so is open again).

exitCode.description:
An approval that ran: its exit code (absent when a signal or the timeout ended it) and the end of its output,
with every injected secret value scrubbed.

finishedAt.description: An approved command: when its result came back (ran or failed), so a client can say how long it took.

gated.description: approval of a gated run: exactly the bytes the node runs.

permission.description: approval of a session's tool prompt, instead of a gated run.

playbook.description: approval of a retro playbook change (an older approval only), instead of a gated run or a tool prompt.

text.description: One line on why the lead needs it.

compare.description:
The same numbers for the compare period. Present on every insight when a compare period was asked for,
also when the rule fired in only one of the two.

firedIn.description: Which periods the rule fired in, with a compare period.

numbers.description: The numbers the message was built from (durations in ms).

spanIds.description: At most 200; `time_spans { rule }` lists them all.

IntakeRef.description:
Something an order or note points at: a file of the project, another order, or a PR. The hub renders these into
the lead's wake as a "References:" block.

oneOf.description: Repo-relative.
A permission prompt waits on a person.
Usage limit: resumes at the reset.

LastMerged.description: The project's latest merge, as the train recorded it.

title.description: The work's own title (its writer task's), not the PR's branch.

parked.description: M4: the lead thread hit a usage limit; derived from the usage layer when read.

threadId.description: The current lead thread on the project's machine; earlier ones stay on the node as history.

fresh.description: Start a fresh lead thread from the current digest (sessionGeneration goes up); the old one stays as history.

parked.description: M4: the lead thread hit a usage limit; derived from the usage layer when read.

threadId.description: The current lead thread on the project's machine; earlier ones stay on the node as history.

LiveLane.description: One lane's live values. In a frame that is not `full`, only lanes that changed are sent.

activity.description: Absent: nothing to say (no run active, or no recent model output; the UI says no more than the status).

spark.description: Absent: unchanged since the last frame (always present in a `full` frame for lanes that have one).

LoginKind.description: Read from the runner's login kind, never from credentials.

label.description: The secret's key, or the tool for a permission prompt.

boxPubKey.description:
M8: the node's X25519 key from its hello; clients seal this machine's secrets to it. Absent: it takes no
secrets.

degradedReason.description: Plain language, set while status is "degraded".

lastSlept.description: The machine's latest sleep its node reported on waking.

cloneRoot.description:
Where a clone onto this machine goes by default: the first of ~/src, ~/code, ~/projects that exists, else
~/src. Absolute.

problem.description: Why this machine could not be scanned (offline, an older node), with its fix.

Marker.description: A change to a figure's denominator, shown next to it.

MergeRules.description: How the default branch may be merged into.

protected.description: Branch protection or an active ruleset applies to the default branch.

requiredReviews.description: Approving reviews a pull request needs.

rulesets.description: Active rulesets that apply to the default branch, by name.

squashAllowed.description: Absent when gh could not read the repository settings.

strict.description: Pull requests must be up to date with the base before merging.

oneOf.description: Derived: at least one item done and every item done or dropped.

MilestoneView.description: A milestone with its derived figure.

firstItemAt.description: The first item's time; scope changes within 10 minutes of it carry no marker.

NotifyPolicy.description:
When a client may interrupt the human with an event marked `attention`. Quiet windows are absolute times the
hub computes from `policy.quiet_hours` in `policy.tz`: the one under way (if any) and the next.

coalesceSec.description: At most one notification per this many seconds; what arrives meanwhile is folded into the next.

quiet.description:
Only "urgent" events notify inside these; empty when quiet hours are off. Ask again after the last one ends
or on decision.recorded.

OrderCard.description: One order (workstream) as the board shows it.

lanes.description: Active first, then newest; finished lanes are left out on the board.

settled.description: Agents done, failed or cancelled, of `total`.

decisions.description: Active decisions scoped to it. Absent from older hubs.

lead.description: Its project's lead (shared by every order of the project); absent when the project has none.

requests.description: Its open secret and approval requests.

steers.description: Its steers (to the lead or one of its tasks) with their receipts, newest first. Absent from older hubs.

workstream.description: Its record: the brief and its done-when. Absent from older hubs.

OrderPhase.description: An order's phase: the first match in this order wins, and the board sorts by it.

oneOf.description: An open ask for it, or a lane waiting on a permission.
An implementer or reader lane starting or working.
A Change reviewing, or a reviewer or qa lane working.
A Change ready, rebasing, in CI or merging.
Never produced now that a lead closes its work; stays until the app stops naming it.
Only queued lanes.
Draft, or running with no tasks while the lead works.
Anything else open: waiting for the lead.

orders.description: By phase, then most recently updated.

PatchId.description: Full lowercase hex patch id, 40 or 64 characters

PeriodBreakdown.description: The numbers of one period, for a comparison.

Placeholder.description: A `{{name}}` the code fills in. A required one missing from an edit gets a warning.

PlanChange.description: One marker: a recorded change to a figure's denominator, never a silent jump.

oneOf.description: A lead's add, edit or drop that moved an open milestone's total after its planning window.
Older markers only: a later claim failed a check a done item listed.
Items dropped by the hub when their order finished, stopped or failed.
A milestone finished and left the project's figure.
An item was added to a done milestone.

PlanGetOutput.description: A plan as `plan show` and `plan_get` return it: derived state, figures and markers.

workstreamId.description: Set when the view is one order's items.

after.description: Items that must be done before this one starts: serial gates.

evidence.description: What verified it, e.g. "#212 merged by the train".

oneOf.description: Set only by the hub, from verification.

PlanLinks.description: What ties work to an item. An item with no links never counts done.

prs.description: PRs listed on the item (`--pr`, or `change enqueue --item`).

tasks.description: Tasks spawned with `--item`; their Changes count through `Change.task_id`.

PlaybookGateChange.description:
A retro playbook change that relaxes a gate (fewer reviewers, a weaker or removed check, a looser rule). The retro is
gone: only an older approval carries one, and the app still shows it.

diff.description: The exact unified diff that applies on approve.

summary.description:
The change in plain words, rendered by the hub for the person: "Bugfixes, medium-size work: reviewers 1 → 0".
The app shows it as the item's label; `diff` only behind expand or copy.

PlaybookName.description: The prefixes `bug:`/`fix:` and `research:` pick bugfix and research.

PlaybookRef.description: <playbook name>@<full lowercase hex git blob SHA>

PrAuthor.description: Who wrote the PR: fleetd's agent when one did, and the GitHub account it was opened from.

laneId.description: The writing agent's lane in the agents view.

login.description: GitHub login; absent when GitHub wasn't reached.

PrCheck.description: One check run or commit status on the head. fleetd's own merge statuses are left out: `queue` says the same.

PrChip.description: One PR on a train strip.

position.description: 0-based; absent for the head (being rebased, checked or merged) and for PRs merged today.

nextOffset.description: Pass back as `offset` for the next page; absent on the last.

noDiff.description: GitHub shows no diff for this file (binary, or too large).

diffLines.description: Lines `pr_diff` pages through; absent when GitHub shows no diff for it (binary, or too large).

path.description: Repo-relative; the new path of a rename.

headSha.description: The head these files are of.

nextOffset.description: Pass back as `offset` for the next page; absent on the last.

body.description: The PR's description, at most 8000 characters. Secrets are replaced by `[secret]`.

history.description: Its moves through the merge queue, newest first.

reviews.description: Newest first: agent verdicts and people's reviews.

mergeCommit.description: The squash commit on the base, once merged.

githubError.description: GitHub couldn't be reached: the list holds only the PRs fleetd records, without checks. Why, and what to do.

PrQueue.description: Where the PR stands in fleetd's merge queue. Absent from a PR fleetd doesn't land.

length.description: PRs waiting in the same queue.

position.description: 0-based place in the queue; absent when not waiting in it.

reason.description: Why it is held or was sent back: a conflict, failing check names, or the refusal's fix.

PrQueueStep.description: One move of the PR through the merge queue.

position.description: 0-based place in its train's queue; absent when not queued.

reviewsDone.description: Clean reviews of the current patch.

reviewsNeeded.description: One for every PR the train lands.

taskId.description: The task that opened it (its writer), when the hub knows: the board groups the PR's checkers under it.

PrReviewEntry.description: One review: an agent's verdict with its findings, or a person's review on GitHub.

agent.description: The reviewing agent (reviewer or QA); absent for a person's review.

blocking.description: Findings that must be fixed before merging; agent reviews only.

current.description: It reviewed the PR's current change (an agent review stays current across a rebase that changes nothing).

login.description: GitHub login of a person's review.

text.description: The agent's findings, or the person's review text. Secrets are replaced by `[secret]`.

PrRow.description: One PR as the list shows it.

title.description: GitHub's title; the writing agent's task title when GitHub wasn't reached.

workstreamId.description: The work it belongs to, when fleetd's agents wrote it.

ProfileTotal.description:
One task profile's part of a scope's agent time and usage, from the spans kept (`coverage.detailSince` on): the
tasks that ran on it, and the lead's spans under high.

outputTokens.description: What claude reported for its messages.

Progress.description: A figure. `pct` counts verified must items by size only; polish shows beside it.

done.description: Must items done and in the figure.

marker.description: The latest scope change, e.g. "↓ from 80% · +3 items: time inspector added".

pct.description: floor(100 · must points done / must points open or done); the polish figure when there are no must items.

polishDone.description: Polish items done and in the figure ("polish 2/5").

text.description: "CI failed on #212", "+2 items: time inspector added".

ProgressEstimate.description:
A project's two-tone bar: solid is what fleetd verified, lighter is credit for work in flight. Every stage it
credits is one fleetd observed (an event, a PR or a CI state), never an agent's word, and nothing in it is a time.

inFlightPct.description: The lighter part: credit for open units' reached stages, plus in-stage credit for the time work on them ran.

pct.description: verified + in flight, floored; 100 only when everything is verified.

verifiedPct.description: The solid part: points verified over points counted.

ProgressPoint.description: One point of a project's series: its bar over time, oldest first.

drop.description: Set when the figure fell at this point; it never falls without one.

paused.description:
Set while the figure holds because the work in flight paused, waiting for an answer or for a usage limit to
reset ("paused: an agent hit a usage limit"). A marker, not a drop: what was earned stays.

useExisting.description: With `url`: when the destination is already a checkout of the same repository, add it instead of failing.

addId.description: A clone was started: its `project.clone_progress`, `project.added` and `project.add_failed` events carry it.

clone.description: A dry run with url: where it would clone, and whether that folder already holds a checkout.

created.description: False when the directory was already a project (it is renamed when a title is given), and in a dry run.

inspect.description: For a path, at once; for a clone, on `project.added`; for a dry run, the repository's facts.

path.description: The project's directory (the clone's destination for a url).

projectId.description: Absent while a clone runs: `project.added` carries it.

ProjectChatState.description: One chat's state, for the sidebar and the status row.

lastSeq.description: The newest message's `seq`; 0 for an empty chat.

needsYou.description: The lead's last message waits for a human reply, or an inline item is open.

machineId.description: Scan only this machine; absent: every machine.

best.description: The machine a clone goes to by default: online, runner ready, fewest running threads. Absent: none is.

query.description: Without projectId: only projects whose title or path contains it.

ProjectGetOutput.description: The projects, or one project's outcome (its fields at the top level).

mediumAllowed.description: Whether the lead may run a task on the medium profile (`project_set`); absent from older hubs, where it is on.

taskCounts.description: Absent until the project has a task.

threads.description: Newest activity first. Task threads are left out; they show under `tasks`.

trains.description: The merge trains of the project's repos; absent until one of its PRs was enqueued.

truncated.description: True when `threads`, `workstreams` or `tasks` was trimmed to its limit.

workstreams.description: Open workstreams (not done, stopped or failed), newest first.

ProjectInspect.description: What a project's checkout or repository says: the default branch, CI and merge rules, and one line on what the lead will need.

leadNeeds.description: One line for a person, e.g. "no CI found: the merge train holds its PRs until the repo has CI".

notes.description: What could not be read, e.g. "branch rules need admin access on acme/storefront".

repo.description: Absent for a checkout without a GitHub remote.

ProjectProblem.description: Why something could not be done, and the one step that fixes it.

oneOf.description: The machine's node is not connected.
No connected machine runs agents.
gh is missing or logged out where it ran.
gh is logged in but cannot see the repository (private, renamed, or a typo).
The path does not exist on the machine.
The path exists but is not a git checkout.
The clone destination exists. `CloneTarget.sameRemote` says whether it is already this repository.
git clone failed; the message is git's own last line.
The machine's node is older than this hub and cannot do this.

ProjectRowState.description: What a project is doing, in one word.

oneOf.description: Agents are running, or its PRs are in review, CI or the train.
The lead is waiting for your reply.

Something outside the work stops it: its machine is offline, at its usage limit or short of disk or CPU for new
agents, or main CI is red.
Nothing running and nothing waiting.

ProjectStatusRow.description: One project on the Status screen: a state word, the two-tone bar, agents running and the last merge.

agentsRunning.description: Its task agents holding a slot now (the lead's own turn is not one).

blockedReason.description: Blocked only: why, in one line, for the expanded row.

progress.description: The project's bar, under the drop rule of its series (status_get). Absent when it has nothing to count.

stale.description: Set when a source the row reads (its machine, its repos on GitHub, their merge train) went quiet.

message.description: The system line it wrote into the chat.

PromptDetail.description: `prompt_get`: every level of one prompt for the asked project (or hub-wide).

perProject.description: False for a one-shot: it has the hub-wide level only.

projectRef.description: The texts in effect for this project; absent: hub-wide.

orphans.description: Without an id: your edits to prompts a release retired, hub-wide ones and the asked project's.

PromptId.description: Prompt registry id, dotted lowercase words

PromptKind.description: How the text reaches the model.

oneOf.description: The first message of a session.
A later message into a running session.
The input of a tool-less one-shot `claude -p`. None ships now; kept while the app names its group.
The human's custom instructions, appended to every lead and task first message.

PromptOverride.description: A human's override: its text and the default it was edited from (absent for a hand-made file).

PromptRef.description: <prompt id>@<10 lowercase hex of the text's git blob SHA>

PromptScope.description: Which text is meant: the one shipped in the binary, the hub-wide override, or one project's override.

base.description: The default ref the text was edited from (`prompt_get` default.ref); absent: the one shipped now.

dryRun.description: Return the warnings without saving; with reset, the ref that would be in effect, without resetting.

reset.description:
True deletes your text at this scope (or your edit to a prompt fleetd retired), so the next level applies.
Only an explicit reset does that: a missing text is an error, never a reset.

text.description: The text to save. May be empty only for `instructions`. Required unless `reset` is true.

warnings.description: What the edit may break; it is saved anyway.

overrideRef.description: The override in effect, when `scope` is not `default`.

scope.description: Which text is in effect for the asked project (or hub-wide).

PromptWarning.description: What an edit may break. Never a refusal: the text is saved anyway.

rule.description: `safety_rule_missing`: the rule's id and who still enforces it.

n.description: Runs in a row with no edit between them.

RequestKind.description:
What a lead needs a person for that chat can't carry safely: a secret value (entered in a masked field and sealed to
the sink's node, never in a transcript), or an approval of a risky command (a gated run, or a session's tool
prompt). The lead asks everything else in chat.

RequestState.description:
The state names of the chat items that show it (`SecretRequestState`, `CommandApprovalState`). secret: open →
stored | withdrawn. approval: open → approved → ran | failed, or open → denied; an approval the node could not run
goes back to open with the reason in `evidence`.

RetiredPromptOverride.description:
An override of a prompt a release retired (merged into another, or replaced by fixed text), kept so the human can
carry what they wrote into a prompt that still exists. Its file stays until `prompt_set` with `reset: true` on its id.

suggestedTarget.description: The prompt that now covers what this one said, when one does. fleetd never copies the text over itself.

why.description: What replaced it, in one line.

oneOf.description: Nothing asks for a review.
Reviews are asked for or running.

done.description: Clean agent reviews of the current change.

needed.description: Agent reviews it needs before it can merge: 1 for a PR fleetd lands, else 0.

SafetyRule.description: A rule the default text carries, found in a text by `needle` (a case-insensitive regex).

present.description: In `PromptDetail`: whether the effective text still matches `needle`.

SecretFingerprint.description: 8 lowercase hex characters: the sha256 prefix of the plaintext

SecretRequest.description: A secret request: the secret's name and where the node writes it.

envName.description: An env: sink's variable, when not the one the key names (`secret_env_name`).

fingerprint.description: Set once the node has written the sink; the value itself never reaches the hub in plain text.

key.description: The secret's name, a dotted slug such as "stripe.test_key".

SecretRequestItem.description:
The lead needs a secret. The app shows a masked field; the value never enters the transcript: it is sealed to the
sink's machine and answered with `secret_submit`, naming `requestId`. Only its fingerprint comes back.

by.description: The key name of the person who answered.

envName.description: An `env:` sink: the variable it writes, when not the one `name` gives (`secrets::secret_env_name`).

note.description: Why it is open again, or why it could not be stored.

text.description: One line: why the lead needs it.

sealed.description: Sealed in the desktop app to the sink machine's `box_pub_key` (see Machine).

SessionPrompt.description: `session_prompt_get`: exactly what a session was told at its start.

disallowedTools.description: Tools the claude runner never offers a fleetd session.

textSha.description: The text's full git blob SHA.

SessionPromptRef.description: One prompt a session pinned at its start; every later message to it renders from this text.

SleptSpan.description: A span a machine spent asleep, epoch milliseconds; `machine.slept` carries the same fields as its data.

cap.description: The fleet cap: agents running at once across every project.

maxAgents.description:
The most of the project's agents (its tasks: writers, readers, reviewers) that run at once; its lead is not
one. The fleet `cap` until set.

queued.description: Its agents waiting for a slot, paused ones included.

running.description: Its agents running now. Above `maxAgents` right after the cap was lowered: nothing is stopped for it.

Span.description: A stored span, as the tools return it.

exclMs.description: Exclusive time: the part no child covers. Absent while open and on envelopes.

itemId.description: The item id in the thread (claude's tool_use or message id), for `thread_window`.

SpanExtra.description: Small per-kind facts. Every field is optional and bounded.

answeredBy.description: Who answered, e.g. a key's label. Never a secret.

check.description: `ci.check`: the check name and its page.

claudeMs.description: `tool.*`: claude's own figure for the call, when the result carries one.

httpStatus.description: `wait.retry.api`: the HTTP status claude retried on.

nodeStartMs.description: The node's own start stamp, kept when the clock offset was above 100 ms.

reason.description: Free text from the source, e.g. a queue reason or a stop reason.

requestId.description: `wait.permission`: the node's request id, joined to the hub's approval request.

statedDelayMs.description: `wait.retry.*`: the delay claude or the node announced. The span is the real wait.

tool.description: The tool's name, for tool and permission spans.

SpanKind.description:
What a span measures. Each kind belongs to exactly one [`Category`]. The code is the stored integer and
never changes; new kinds take new codes.

oneOf.description: A run's envelope, lifecycle started to its end. Its leaves tile it; it has no exclusive time of its own.
One assistant message, from the previous visible stream event to `message_stop`.
Previous visible stream event to `message_start`: claude-local work, network, API queueing and prefill.
Read, Grep, Glob, LS.
Edit, MultiEdit, Write, NotebookEdit.
Overlapping tool calls from one message; the calls are its children.
Train git, and agent Bash whose program is `git` or `gh`.
Time inside a run that no other span covers: claude-local work between stream events.
A write waiting in the hub's queue for an offline machine.
Older hubs only: a writer waiting for an area lease. Kept so their spans still read.
A send waiting behind the session's active run.
A permission prompt, inside its tool span; `extra.decidedBy` says who answered.
A secret or approval request, opened to settled.
Waiting in the train's line.
One check run, GitHub's own `started_at` to `completed_at`.
The train's push to the check's start.
needs_rebase or ci_failed until the next head.
Intake, from submit to placed.
Lost data: spans the node dropped or the hub could not take. `extra.count` says how many.
Still open when it was cut, e.g. a check still running when a red one decided.

Spark.description:
Work per 2 s bucket, oldest first, ending with the bucket that ends at `end_at`. A sample is
`min(255, 16 × items started + streamed chars / 32 + output tokens not streamed as text / 8)`; a bucket with
no frames is 0.

StaleMark.description: Why a part is not live: its source went quiet past its cadence.

reason.description: "no heartbeat from devbox for 4m", "GitHub not reached for 4m: …".

since.description: The source's last good signal (a heartbeat, a GitHub answer, a train pass).

StalePrompt.description:
An override edited from an older default than the one this release ships. It stays in effect until the human
saves it again with `base` = `current.ref`, or resets it.

base.description: The default it was edited from; absent when the file has no `base` or that text is unknown to this hub.

merged.description: A line 3-way merge of base → current into yours; with `<<<<<<<` markers where they conflict.

series.description:
With projectRef: the bar over time, oldest first: why it fell (`drop`) and when it held on paused work
(`paused`).

ackExcerpt.description: Acknowledged: the agent's reply, first 200 characters.

detail.description:
Plain words on the stage: "waiting for lab-b (until 14:30)", "held: usage resets 14:00", the failure, or
"sent (node older than 0.9)" when the node cannot report receipts.

planChange.description: A plan change the steer made, e.g. "−1 item".

runId.description: The node run id it was sent as; also the user message id in the thread.

seenAt.description: The first model request that carried it.

stoppedTool.description: `how = stopped`: one line on the step it stopped.

workstreamId.description: The order it belongs to (a task's own order for a task steer).

SteerMode.description: How a steer reaches a running agent.

oneOf.description:
Enter, "add to the lead's queue": taken in at the agent's next tool boundary, as its own turn. Never cuts a
running tool.
⌘Enter, "interrupt and redirect now": stops the current step and delivers at once.

ackExcerpt.description: Acknowledged: the agent's reply, first 200 characters.

detail.description:
Plain words on the stage: "waiting for lab-b (until 14:30)", "held: usage resets 14:00", the failure, or
"sent (node older than 0.9)" when the node cannot report receipts.

planChange.description: A plan change the steer made, e.g. "−1 item".

runId.description: The node run id it was sent as; also the user message id in the thread.

seenAt.description: The first model request that carried it.

stoppedTool.description: `how = stopped`: one line on the step it stopped.

workstreamId.description: The order it belongs to (a task's own order for a task steer).

oneOf.description: The hub stored it, or put it in the offline queue.
claude's context took it in (`command_lifecycle started`).
The agent replied after taking it in, or a lead call named it (`--steer S12`).
Its run ended with no reply after it was delivered.
Dropped while still queued.
The machine stayed offline past the queue's TTL.

SteerTarget.description: Who a steer is for: an order's lead, or one task (writer, reviewer, …).

ackExcerpt.description: Acknowledged: the agent's reply, first 200 characters.

detail.description:
Plain words on the stage: "waiting for lab-b (until 14:30)", "held: usage resets 14:00", the failure, or
"sent (node older than 0.9)" when the node cannot report receipts.

planChange.description: A plan change the steer made, e.g. "−1 item".

runId.description: The node run id it was sent as; also the user message id in the thread.

seenAt.description: The first model request that carried it.

stoppedTool.description: `how = stopped`: one line on the step it stopped.

workstreamId.description: The order it belongs to (a task's own order for a task steer).

itemId.description: The plan item it was spawned for (`--item`).

parked.description: M4: its thread hit a usage limit; the task is idle until fleetd sends "continue" at `resumeAt`.

pr.description: The PR a review task reviews. Required at spawn for review; absent on older rows (hub-spawned judges).

profile.description: Resolved at spawn. Rows stored with a model and effort read as `high` (the hub migrates its own).

queuedReason.description: Why it is queued, e.g. "fleet cap: 40 of 40 running".

TaskCounts.description: A project's tasks by state, all time.

TaskKind.description: Only write tasks get a worktree.

TaskProfile.description:
What an agent runs on. There are exactly two, both claude-opus-5-5: `high` (effort high) is the default and what
the lead, every reviewer and every helper call run; `medium` (effort medium) is for mechanical tasks the lead picks.

tail.description: The latest assistant message, trimmed to its last 2000 characters.

effort.description: As reported by the runner; not narrowed to Effort because it may report other levels.

headline.description: First line of the latest visible assistant text.

focus.description: The index of `itemId` in `items`; absent when the node no longer has it.

byProfile.description: High first; absent when no task or lead span is in the period.

storedBytes.description: The hub's span tables on disk.

oneOf.description: The project's lead sessions, split across orders by the workstreams each wake served.
Includes the task's subagents (tasks it spawned).

nextAfterId.description: Absent when there are no more.

Tokens.description: Summed over the lane's runs. `live`: the running run's usage is streaming in (else it updates at each run's end).

ToolPermission.description:
An approval raised by a session's tool permission prompt instead of a gated command: answering it answers the prompt
on the project's node. Its machine is the request's project's.

summary.description: The command, the path, or the tool's own description.

TrainLive.description: One repo's merge train, resolved for the strip: head first, then the queue in order, then today's merges.

head.description: The Change being rebased, checked or merged now.

UsageBreaker.description: Open: no new turns start on the machine's login until `until` or usage_resume.

message.description: The plain notice, as the usage.breaker event said it.

until.description: Absent while open means until usage_resume.

UsageClass.description:
What stopped a turn. `usage_limit`: the plan's usage limit or a proxy cooldown, with a reset. `rate_limit`: a 429.
`pool_exhausted`: the user's proxy has no account for the model; it waits for usage_resume.

UsageParked.description: A task or lead whose thread hit a limit; fleetd sends it one "continue" at `resume_at`.

resumeAt.description: Absent for pool_exhausted: it resumes on usage_resume.

lastEvents.description: The latest thread.usage_limited, usage.breaker and usage.resumed events for the machine, oldest first.

catchUp.description: What to do with a firing missed while the hub was down.

createdBy.description: keyId of the agent key that set it.

nextRunAt.description: Absent once the wake is done or cancelled.

WakeCron.description: Standard 5-field cron; the hub parses it.

oneOf.description: Counts toward the headline number.
Shown beside the number, never in it.

WorkAction.description: A command, file edit or tool call. Secrets in its summary and output are replaced by `[secret]`.

WorkMessage.description: A message the agent or its person wrote. Secrets are replaced by `[secret]`.

text.description: The last 2000 characters of a longer message.

WorkStep.description: One step of an agent's work.

playbook.description: Pinned at creation. Absent on workstreams from before M9.

by.description: Who submitted it: an agent keyId, "human" or "lead:<machineId>/<projectId>".

oneOf.description: Never set now that a lead closes its work; old records were moved back to running.
